title: Evidence Chain
intent: Pick up a witness and Dr. Lina at a clinic, protect the sealed archive and choose an air or armoured extraction.
observed: The opening centres the escort on the divided boulevard, with clinic pickup and extraction destinations outside the immediate view. The broader route is dominated by wreckage and sand intrusions, so the protected medical/evidence journey has little distinct scenery support.
camera: Frame the escort/APC together, then give a brief camera-only view of the clinic entrance and both extraction choices. Keep the witness pickup clear of foreground roofs and the HUD.
light: Preserve readable people at the clinic and against the APC; use restrained cool medical accents against the warm settlement, without a new overall colour grade.
ground: Create an accessible clinic forecourt and a legible pickup crossover to the existing roadway. Give the helicopter receiving area a clear, appropriately surfaced pad and shoulder rather than relying on surrounding sand.
props: Use a small medical receiving cluster, a shaded waiting spot, physical archive cases and an extraction-side staging group. Keep medical activity separate from wreck dressing; no extra functional helicopter or APC duplicates.
landscape: Consolidate roadside wreck clusters so the two evacuation paths remain visually legible; blend the clinic parcel with the street rather than leaving an isolated white slab.

title: Network Break
intent: Breach a verified bunker gate, stop an erasure node and recover an audit while protecting neighbouring homes.
observed: The compound closely repeats Breach Assault: a bare sandy enclosure, a dish, a small building and two watchtowers. The bunker/erasure/audit sequence is not strongly expressed by the architecture or ground, and the gate sits close to the top edge in the opening view.
camera: Frame gate and first squad together, then use a camera-only step through the authorised targets and protected homes. Keep the protected side of the block visible without implying an attack command.
light: Keep target entries readable in shadow; use material value and controlled equipment accents to distinguish the secured installation from civilian roofs.
ground: Connect gate, erasure node and archive with a maintained service strip. Finish the boulevard-to-compound crossing and give the bunker entrance a grounded reinforced threshold inside its existing footprint.
props: Differentiate this mission from the earlier relay compound with armoured entry details, cooling units, cable conduits, equipment cabinets and a clearly secured archive entrance. Dress protected homes domestically and retain their existing ownership and destruction behavior.
landscape: Use rock contact and retaining detail to make the bunker look embedded rather than placed on sand; avoid adding inaccessible steps or altering the verified breach route.

title: Air Corridor
intent: Defend an operating medical flight corridor with linked radar and missile coverage on two approaches.
observed: The opening mostly shows a roadside launcher and pale apron; the radar/air-defense relationship is not visually obvious. Inspection shows large repeated slabs, sparsely organised aircraft servicing space and an abrupt, minimally marked runway end.
camera: Frame radar and the first launcher together, then provide a camera-only overview of west and north approaches. Maintain enough altitude for aircraft context without reducing ground units to dots.
light: The enabled-light probe confirms one active source sun and disabled Match lights for this airfield binding. Preserve that ownership; improve apron/aircraft contrast locally rather than adding lights.
ground: Apply the runway-end treatment shared with Airlift: threshold/end markings, shoulder bands, restrained touchdown wear and deliberate transitions. Separate taxiway yellow guidance from road markings and link apron exits cleanly to actual taxiways.
props: Give radar a small service/generator cluster and the medical-flight area a distinct receiving shelter, ambulance-side staging and orderly ground equipment. Keep missile launch envelopes, runway and aircraft circulation clear.
landscape: Organise perimeter vegetation and stones outside air operations surfaces; reduce the uniformly repeated small ground specks at tactical distance.
